newsitem.title: FRANCE: Algerians urged to vote to change constitution.
newsitem.headline: Algerians urged to vote to change constitution.

text.p: Algerians have been called by President Liamine Zeroual to vote on November 28 to change their constitution.
The main changes are to allow political parties but ban those based on religion and language, limit the president to two five-year terms, and confirm Islam as the state religion.
The authorities say the reforms will help end Algeria's crisis sparked by the January 1992 cancellation of elections dominated by Moslem fundamentalists. An estimated 60,000 people have been killed.
Here are the main milestones leading to the ballot:
January 31, 1994 - Zeroual appointed head of state.
August - President starts dialogue with five opposition parties amid hopes that jailed leaders of radical Islamists might join. Secular opposition parties stay away.

September - Hopes of deal with Islamic Salvation Front (FIS) detained chief Abbas Madani collapsed after the authorities found letter on body of Cherif Gousmi, leader of Armed Islamic Group (GIA), from Madani's deputy Ali Belhadj urging increased killings.
October - Zeroual breaks off talks, says presidential election will be held in 1995. Blasts FIS leaders for "intransigency".
November 16, 1995 - Zeroual wins first multi-candidate presidential poll with more than 60 percent of vote.
April 1996 - Zeroual resumes talks with politicians and personalities. Radical Islamists excluded.

May - Zeroual unveils blueprint of political reforms with plans for proportional representation, a parliament with two legislative chambers and ban on parties using Islam to gain power. Pledges referendum to be held this year, followed by general elections early in 1997, then local elections. Main opposition secular Socialist Forces Front dismisses plan.
July - Zeroual resumes talks with parties.
August - Talks conclude with draft laws proposed to introduce proportional representation, ban religious parties, and underline that Islam is religion of the state.
September - After more talks in July and August, Zeroual announces Sept 14 and 15 as dates for conference to adopt his reform plan.
October - Zeroual sets referendum date - November 28.
